title: About Access Policies Defined by My Tenant

blocks.text: Access policy rules can be created by the guest partner admin for Business-to-Business (B2B) Federation for shared access to your tenant's applications. This article describes access policy rules that are defined by your tenant. To learn more about access policy rules that are created by your partner, see About Access Policies Defined by Partners.
Access policies defined by your tenant provide the following benefits and enable you to:

blocks.item: Manage access policies for both internal applications and B2B federated applications from a single place.
Maintain full ownership and control over who can access your applications, whether you are acting as a host or a guest tenant.
Enforce your organization's security standards and compliance requirements across all access.

blocks.heading: About the Defined by My Tenant Page

blocks.text: On the Defined by My Tenant page, you can create and manage access policy rules for internal applications and users, as well as applications federated by the host.
On the Defined by My Tenant page (Private Access > Policy > Access Policy > Rules > Defined by My Tenant), you can do the following:

blocks.item: View a list of policy groups or rules.
View the total rules, total policy groups, number of enabled rules, and number of disabled rules for the information that appears in the table.
Modify the columns displayed in the table.
Click the Filter icon to show or hide the filters. The number displayed in parentheses next to the icon indicates the number of applied filters.
Filter the information that appears in the table. By default, no filters are applied. To learn more, see Using Tables.
View a list of all configured access policy rules. For each rule, you can see:

Rule Order: The policy evaluation order number for the rule. Private Access (ZPA) applies policy rules based on the order they are listed here. To change the rule order, go to the Global Rules or Policy Groups page, and click the rule order number and manually enter a new value.

Updating the rule order of an access policy configured using Zscaler Deception is not supported. When changing the rule order of a regular access policy and there is an access policy configured using Deception, the rule order of the regular access policy must be greater than the rule order for an access policy configured using Deception.
Rule Name: The name of the rule.
Policy Groups: The name of the policy group that the policy rule is associated with.
Rule Action: Indicates the action for the rule (i.e., Allow Access, Block Access, or Require Approval).
Status: Indicates if the rule is enabled or disabled.
Display more rows or a different page of the table.
Go to the Defined by Partners page to view access policy rules that are defined by your partners for your federated applications.
